calls.submitted_prompt:
Create one detailed scientific overview illustration titled "From Wins to Worth". This is a conceptual raster figure for a paper about the Indiana Fever professional basketball franchise, explaining how capacity-censored audience demand becomes ticket revenue and enters financially constrained roster decisions through time. Use a 3:2 landscape canvas, pure white background, restrained scientific color, and English labels throughout. Intended placement is the end of the Introduction before model definitions; intended printed width is approximately 180 mm. Draw a unified arena-and-accounting scene with enough physical and mathematical detail to explain the operations when the headings are hidden. Keep the short title at the upper left and "Conceptual schematic" at the upper right. The instructions below describe the complete composition; they are not text to print on the figure.

PURPOSE, SCOPE, AND SOURCE AUTHORITY

The main visual claim is that observed attendance is limited by available seats, whereas underlying demand may exceed them; a capped-demand forecast and a separate pricing decision determine ticket receipts, and those receipts affect profit, cash, franchise valuation, debt adjustment, and the feasible roster action at the next decision time. Concentrate on this mechanism. Show the same club, venue, accounts, and named state components throughout. The drawing must distinguish a ticket price from a franchise valuation, an operating earnings proxy from net profit, and every income or earnings quantity from the stock of available cash. A full arena is evidence of a capacity boundary, not a direct measurement of how much demand exists beyond that boundary.

The content authority is the pinned manuscript "From Wins to Worth: A Quantitative Model of Performance, Attendance, Revenue, and Valuation for Sports Teams", 2026 problem D. Physical pages 9-12 establish Elo and censored attendance; 12-15 give pricing, accounting, valuations and leverage; 15-18 give actions and rolling decisions; 19-24 expose specification ambiguities. This overview contains no numerical results, team branding or new financial calculation.

Preserve source ambiguities: occupancy-rule pricing and assumed-elasticity optimization are alternative descriptions, not one fitted model. Section 7.2 asserts valuation aggregation without weights; later equations use revenue multiples and section 11 defers EBITDA/DCF calibration. Show separate lenses and basis-dependent V. Injury is an exogenous strength shift because stochastic injury is both claimed and deferred. Retain the ledger's EBI as an operating proxy and label its valuation lens "EBITDA proxy"; do not resolve the manuscript's terminology by inventing accounting terms.

ONE COMPOSITION: A CUTAWAY ARENA OPENS INTO ITS BOOKS

Use an asymmetric composition: arena and demand mechanism at left, about 50 percent of width and the upper two thirds; accounting and valuation at upper/middle right, about 43 percent of width; a shallow time register along the lower quarter. These are allocations, not panel boxes. Read from pre-game records to seats and capacity, ticket multiplication, ledger, cash/debt register, then roster decision. Return only to the next-time state.

Draw the arena as a broad three-quarter cutaway with an open front, an oval bowl of individually readable seat rows, two or three internal concourse levels, short aisle breaks, entrance turnstiles, and a simple basketball court. Use the bowl's seats, not the court, as the main visual mass. Give the left/front perimeter a visible finite end so the seat count is physically bounded. The roof is removed, not turned into a complex architecture rendering. The court supplies just enough identity: two half-courts, center circle, restrained line work, and two small hoops. Do not add players, mascots, spectators cheering in the foreground, trophies, confetti, sponsor branding, advertising screens, or a city panorama. These would compete with the scientific boundary. Seats, aisle divisions, admitted ticket stubs, and the remaining possible demand carry the physical detail.

Keep one recognizable venue with its attached seat magnification and demand inset. A front-facing ruled ledger extends into the right region; valuation leaves sit above its right end. The lower roster register is an operations sheet, not a dashboard. Use white space and meaningful brackets for capacity, arithmetic, accounts, time intervals and feasible choices; no decorative outer frame.

THE PRE-GAME INPUT: KNOWN STATE, MATCHUP, AND SCHEDULE

Above the arena's left shoulder, place a short horizontal set of actual game-record slips. One slip has a paired matchup row with two small generic team markers and the label "Pre-game Elo". A second has a minimal schedule strip labeled "Schedule"; use generic positions rather than fabricated dates. A third carries two tiny aligned mark sequences labeled "Popularity". These are joined fields for the same game, not independent networks. Show a thin common alignment rule below them, ending at the label "x_t" beside the demand inset. Their numerical entries remain symbolic. Blank line segments may suggest record structure, but never resemble unreadably small body text or fictitious measurements.

In the matchup slip, two opposed Elo markers have a difference bracket ending at "p(win)". Use no numerical probability or score. Beside the focal team's marker, show a ghosted lower position labeled "Injury scenario". The displacement changes effective strength only; it does not change capacity or financing rates and is not a stochastic injury simulator.

The top strip conditions demand through x_t; do not assert a universally positive win-probability effect on attendance. Observed results return from the time register only to the next available pre-game state. Unknown future scores cannot inform the current price or roster choice.

ARENA SEATS, UNSEEN DEMAND, AND THE CAPACITY BOUNDARY

Enlarge the front-left seat bank, matching the bowl's curvature with two dotted magnification guides. Keep fixed seat backs, bases and side aisles. Teal admission tokens occupy some seats; empty seats preserve pale-gray geometry. Counts are schematic, with no seat numbers or implied attendance rate. A "Capacity C_t" bracket ends on the bank's physical edges, never on the exterior queue.

Next to the entrance, show a narrow stream of candidate ticket stubs. The stubs before admission are thin amber outlines, representing possible underlying demand. Stubs admitted into the bank become teal and attach to seat positions. A faded continuation beyond the gate represents demand that cannot be recovered from a full-house count. Use only a few symbolic stubs, not a literal crowd length. Label the before-gate stream "Latent demand" and the occupied bank "Observed attendance". A vertical capacity stop next to the gate carries C_t and is connected by a dotted association to the seat-bank capacity bracket. This makes the limit intelligible as the same C_t in the physical venue and in the mathematical inset.

The dashed, open-ended continuation is unobserved demand, not a measured waiting list. Within the magnification only, contrast "Below capacity" with "At capacity" using the same seat geometry and an occupancy overlay. This is a schematic condition, not the reported baseline. Do not duplicate the whole arena.

Immediately below this bank, typeset the observation rule "A_t = min(D_t, C_t)". In this local rule D_t is demand, whereas D without t in the accounting region is debt. Keep these visually and linguistically separated: every appearance of D_t beside the distribution must sit under "Latent demand", and the debt register must explicitly say "Debt D". Avoid an anonymous D-only arrow that could refer to either. The corresponding forecast is "Â_t = E[min(D_t, C_t) | x_t]". Preserve the order of min inside the expectation; do not draw min(E[D_t], C_t), an ordinary regression followed by clipping, or mean demand as a fully observed customer count.

THE CENSORED-DEMAND INSET IS PART OF THE ARENA

At the front base of the arena, integrate a medium-size mathematical cutaway of the crowd mechanism. It should be large enough for the cap and tail to read at publication width but remain subordinate to the seats. The inset contains a single smooth, schematic lognormal density above an unnumbered horizontal demand axis. It starts at positive demand, rises to a rounded peak, and has a right tail. The horizontal axis has only the symbolic cap C_t and a short "Demand" label. Mark the vertical cap with a dark restrained line; continue the original distribution beyond it using an amber dashed tail with a faint hatch. Label that side "Censored tail". Do not use data points, gridlines, fitted parameters, empirical confidence bands, or calibrated tick marks.

Draw two slim operand guides below the density. The first collects the continuous part below C_t with the mathematical label "E[D_t 1(D_t < C_t) | x_t]". The second collects the tail into a small filled atom at C_t, labeled "C_t P(D_t ≥ C_t | x_t)". A visible plus sign between these two contributions leads to the forecast label Â_t. This decomposition is an explanatory rewriting of the source's capped expectation, not a new numerical estimator. The tail probability contributes capacity times its mass; it must not disappear, be subtracted, or be counted as extra seats. The atom is on the attendance support at C_t, not a separate peak in the latent-demand density. If the drawing uses a second short support line for the capped attendance distribution, align its C_t exactly beneath the original cap and give that line the label "Attendance".

Print "ln D_t ~ N(μ_t, σ²)" and "μ_t = x_tᵀβ" beside the inset. A small "Censor-aware fit" cue contrasts a non-full observation dot with a near-capacity record's dashed right extension. Near-full records supply tail evidence, not exact latent demand. Omit the operational near-full threshold and ridge-fitting details from the art; the physical cap C_t remains explicit.

Connect x_t to density parameters and associate the seat capacity with the mathematical cap. End the inset at one prominent forecast-seat token Â_t. This forecast leaves for pricing and receipts; keep it typographically distinct from the observed A_t. Seats limit observation without creating latent demand.

PRICING AND TICKET MULTIPLICATION AT THE ARENA EXIT

On the right side of the arena, just before the ledger, draw an actual paired ticket register. Its left operand is the forecast-seat token Â_t and its right operand is a small perforated ticket bearing "p̄_t" and "USD / ticket". Between them is a clean multiplication sign. Below the two operands, a short receipt strip reads "Â_t × p̄_t". A bracket gathers repeated symbolic game receipts into a single home-game subtotal "T_ticket = 10⁻⁶ Σ_home Â_t p̄_t". The subscript home is an explanatory restriction to home ticket revenue, matching the source's home-game use; there is no invented count of home games. The power 10⁻⁶ converts dollars to USD millions. Do not multiply by franchise value, profit, the number of wins, or venue capacity again.

Above the price ticket, a small mechanical selector or folded price schedule shows "ρ̂_t = Â_t / C_t" entering "Occupancy rule" and ending at p̄_t. Draw three short symbolic price levels with an up/down relation, not a numerical price curve; do not print an alleged optimal price. The base-price input is a small perforated stub labeled "Base price". Its edge joins the price selector, not the latent-demand fit. The reader should see which object provides expected quantity and which provides money per admission. Do not use a dollar sign alone as the model. Show the quantity-times-unit-price operation prominently and the price rule as a quieter branch.

Beside the selector, add an "Elasticity scenarios" tab qualified "assumed", with a dashed alternative-specification association. No solid price feedback enters the fitted demand density. This does not jointly execute two pricing methods or add another revenue term. Omit the under-specified season-ticket-conversion stream.

THE OPERATING LEDGER: ACTUAL ADDITIVE AND SUBTRACTIVE TERMS

The ticket receipt enters the upper left margin of a large open ledger on the right. Render the paper surface flat enough that every mathematical row is front-facing. Give it subtle page-edge depth, one visible binding fold, and sparse ruled horizontal rows; do not rotate formulas in perspective. The top two entries read "+ T_ticket" and "+ T_other". The second entry is attached to two small contract slips labeled "Media" and "Sponsorship", with a common bracket labeled "Other revenue". These are evidence carriers for revenue categories, not bank-building icons or floating coins. A sum rule below them produces "T = T_ticket + T_other". All ledger money values use the common unit "USD millions" in its upper margin; there are no invented amounts.

Below total revenue T, place two subtractive rows: "− Sᵖ" with the local label "Salaries", and "− ηT" with the label "Operating costs". Align their minus signs so the operation reads like accounting. Below a fine subtotal rule, write "EBI = T − Sᵖ − ηT" and label the result "Operating proxy". Preserve the fact that operating cost is proportional to revenue and that salary is an additional separate term. Do not merge both into one unlabelled expense slab or subtract salary twice. The salary line has a small receiving port for ΔS from the selected roster action; the operating-cost fraction is not changed by that same action unless the paper says so. Use the same Sᵖ identity on the roster salary field and on this row.

One line below EBI, draw a paired interest calculation as a narrow attached debt note, "I_D = D × r". It takes "Debt D" from the current debt register and "Rate r" from a small input notch. The comprehensive rate is the manuscript's financing rate, conceptually market rate plus spread, without fabricated percentages. Let its result land exactly at the ledger's subtraction row "− I_D". Below a second rule, write "π = EBI − I_D" with the label "Profit". Interest is below operating earnings: an interest-rate increase must not directly subtract from EBITDA/EBI a second time. The ledger is a source-specific simplified book, so do not add tax, depreciation, amortization, capex, working-capital, or retained-earnings lines that are not defined by this mechanism.

Ledger row lengths indicate alignment, not monetary magnitude. Subtotal rules close arithmetic. Use cool income marks, muted warm minus signs, and stronger accents only at constraint contacts. No scaled waterfall or coin stack is needed.

TWO MATCHED ACCOUNTS: CASH AND DEBT ARE SEPARATE STATES

Immediately below the operating ledger, extend a short two-row stock register. The first row reads "Cash_end = Cash_begin + π + b − q"; the second reads "D_end = D + b − q". Both must be easy to read at 180 mm width. Put the same narrow vertical b and q posting tabs across the two rows: b adds to both cash and debt, while q subtracts from both. Label these tabs "Borrow b" and "Repay q". This shared posting geometry is essential. A borrowing entry never enters the revenue sum or the profit subtotal. A repayment entry never reduces EBI or becomes an operating cost. The profit π from the operating ledger feeds only the cash row and the decision evaluation, not the debt row directly.

The label over the cash register is "Simplified cash book". This makes clear that adding π to cash is the paper's approximation rather than a complete statement of cash flows. Draw a thin lower bound under the cash row labeled "Cash_min", and a thin upper bound beside the debt row labeled "D_max". Each boundary belongs to its own account. Do not fill both rows with liquid reservoirs or monetary piles, which would confuse stocks with financial value. A ledger row with a bounded end-state marker is the proper carrier. Put the end-state marker above the cash floor without assigning its height any numerical meaning; the illustration does not certify all candidate states as feasible.

Place "D* = L* V" above the posting tabs. Compare D with D*: borrowing b applies below target; repayment q applies above it, limited by available cash above Cash_min. These are conditional alternatives. Put a "Cash floor" stop on q and print "Cash_end ≥ Cash_min" and "0 ≤ D_end ≤ D_max" by their accounts. No numerical gauge is needed.

Do not print a universal D_end = D* identity. The source's cash-limited repayment rule can leave achieved leverage different from target leverage, even though a later optimization constraint is written as an equality. Show "Target L*" near the selection and "L_end = D_end / V" beside the end-state readout. The target and achieved labels are separate. Do not claim that profit automatically repays debt, that a positive profit guarantees adequate liquidity, or that a high valuation can be spent as cash. If a candidate cannot meet the cash or debt limits, its action record must stop at the feasibility bracket rather than passing into the next state. The picture need not implement a new funding policy to rescue that candidate.

FRANCHISE VALUATION: DISTINCT ESTIMATION LENSES

Above the ledger's far-right end, arrange three small, overlapping valuation leaves with different exposed edges, like pages in a comparison file. They are deliberately unequal in shape and only large enough for a short formula and label. The first leaf says "Revenue multiple" and "V_rev = m_rev T φ(r)". The second says "EBITDA proxy" and "V_ebi = m_ebi EBI φ(r)". The third says "DCF" and has a miniature strip of future FCF entries leading through discount denominators to "V_DCF". A final outlined terminal tab on the DCF strip indicates terminal value. Do not invent a horizon, growth rate, value, or free-cash-flow amount. The DCF strip represents discounted future free cash flows, not the current cash balance.

Use light dotted read guides from T to the revenue-multiple leaf and from EBI to the EBITDA-proxy leaf. They should terminate on the correct operands. The DCF leaf receives a separately named local "FCF" input: there is no automatic π = FCF link and no arrow from Cash_end that declares them identical. Place the rate r as a compact shared condition near these leaves, with one dashed guide reaching the discount-factor notation φ(r) and another reaching the DCF discount strip. The source treats rate as a valuation condition and as an interest-cost input; preserve these two roles. Do not draw interest expense itself as an input that reduces the EBI operand of the EBITDA multiple.

A light brace groups the leaves under "Franchise value". Below the brace, a small readout says "V: basis-dependent". A dotted comparison association, with no plus sign, joins the leaves to this symbolic readout. Add the short qualifier "Aggregation unspecified" beside that association. This denotes that the paper discusses aggregation but does not supply a consistent usable rule. It does not assert that the paper forbids averaging. The V readout supplies the denominator in leverage and the target-debt calculation, and supplies a value criterion in roster choice. There must be no route from V into the cash stock equation as a cash deposit. Keep the valuation leaves visually detached from the admission tickets so that p̄_t, a price per ticket, cannot be mistaken for V, a franchise estimate.

At fixed T and r, the revenue-multiple branch is cost-insensitive; the EBI branch carries salary and operating-cost effects. Keep those read guides distinct. No cost shortcut reaches V_rev, and no numerical valuation or weighted-average result is shown.

ROSTER DECISION AND CHANGING TIME STATES

Use the lower quarter for a continuous operations register with three differently sized elements: a compact known-state row at the left, a central roster-action sheet with feasibility edges, and a next-state row toward the right. Under the register, a thin time line has four small notches corresponding to the paper's four rolling segments. Only one adjacent transition is expanded, labeled "k" and "k+1"; the remaining notches are small and unlabeled. Do not replicate four identical modules. A boundary at the expanded transition separates data already observed from future outcomes. Shade no full-width background band. The chronology comes from notches and the persistent state identities, not from a large decorative loop arrow.

Print "Known state" and "s_k = (E_k, P_k, Cash_k, D_k)" in one four-field row. E is strength, P popularity, and p̄_t alone is ticket price. Already observed game/attendance slips attach to the state. Its fields feed matching pre-game and account operands through identical small port labels, avoiding long crossing cables.

The action sheet is a narrow set of three roster records labeled "NO_MOVE", "SIGN", and "TRADE". They are alternative actions. On each record, show the same operand columns "ΔE", "ΔP", and "ΔS". A blank roster-position outline and a small contract corner can make the records physically meaningful, but do not draw celebrity faces, star ratings, medals, or fabricated contract values. ΔE changes strength, ΔP changes popularity, and ΔS changes salary. Use symbolic increments only. The paper inconsistently uses ΔC and ΔS for salary, so this figure consistently uses ΔS to avoid conflict with arena capacity C_t. Do not copy the inconsistent units and values printed in the source's discussion beneath its player-comparison table.

Candidates meet a feasibility bracket labeled "Salary cap" and "Roster limit", linked to the cash/debt conditions. A symbolic stop indicates rejection without declaring any named candidate infeasible. The selection reads "Choose (a*, L*)" and "Value + profit − risk". This summarizes the objective without invented weights or generated risk distributions.

Selected-action tags "E + ΔE", "P + ΔP", and "Sᵖ + ΔS" reach the respective state fields and salary port. L* reaches target debt L* V. Candidate evaluation reuses the same arena and ledger through named ports. NO_MOVE has zero increments; this drawing does not numerically choose a new action.

After the chosen action and the next observed segment's results, the next-state row is "s_(k+1) = (E_(k+1), P_(k+1), Cash_(k+1), D_(k+1))". It uses exactly the same field ordering, widths, and colors as the earlier state row. Carry the right edge of Cash_end into Cash_(k+1) and D_end into D_(k+1). Carry the updated strength and popularity into their own fields. A small "New observations" slip enters this next-state row only after the time boundary. Place "Re-evaluate" beside a dashed return association from that row to the named next-round input ports. Its arrowhead must not land on the earlier known-state row. The mechanism is a rolling update using available information, not future-informed retrospective optimization.

EXACT CONNECTION REGISTER AND DRAWING PRIORITY

Every connection must reach a named operand. The preceding sections exhaust the topology: features condition demand; capacity clips observations and forecasts; forecast and capacity determine occupancy; forecast and price multiply into receipts; receipts and other revenue sum; costs and interest subtract at their proper levels. Earnings, revenue and independently specified FCF feed their respective valuation lenses. Value enters debt ratios and targets, while borrowing/repayment update matched cash/debt stocks. Feasible actions change strength, popularity and salary, and available observations update the next state. Use repeated named ports where continuous cables would obscure these exact endpoints. No additional automatic arrows are authorized.

Forbidden routes: valuation to cash deposits; borrowing to revenue; repayment to expense; interest to EBI; injury to capacity; future results to current choices; roster/leverage selection to a joint ticket-price optimization. Market-size and league-expansion scenes are outside this overview's focus.

VISUAL GRAMMAR, LABEL CONTROL, AND FINAL APPEARANCE

Use ink navy for text and most mathematical marks, muted teal for admitted seats and revenue-bearing forecast objects, desaturated blue for structural arena detail and known-state fields, quiet amber for unobserved demand and price assumptions, and a restrained terracotta accent for subtractive postings and constraint stops. White remains the dominant background. Grayscale structure must preserve meanings: filled versus outlined admission tokens, solid cap versus dashed tail, plus/minus signs, and labeled account rows must remain distinguishable without hue. Avoid rainbow maps, large pastel zone fills, glowing surfaces, gradients encoding invented values, and glossy app-dashboard styling. A soft local shadow under the arena edge may establish the cutaway; no colored backdrop should masquerade as scientific detail.

Keep finite seats, demand support, ticket operands and ledger rows large; the court remains modest. Fine seat strokes contrast with stronger cap, arithmetic and state-boundary marks. Leave clear whitespace around formulas, the density decomposition and the distinct valuation/cash/debt objects.

Set the title at approximately 15-17 pt equivalent at final width, the four regional labels at 10-11 pt, and primary formulas and object labels around 8-10 pt. The regional labels are "Seats constrain observation", "Tickets to operating earnings", "Cash and debt", and "Decisions through time". They float near the relevant objects rather than becoming colored header bars. Use a clean scientific sans serif for words and a compatible math face for formulas. Legible mathematical subscripts, overbars, hats, inequality signs, expectation brackets, and plus/minus signs have priority over tiny prose. If the composition becomes tight, shorten a subordinate verbal label and remove ornamental detail before shrinking the formulas or converting the main objects into empty boxes.

Print only the specified short labels, formulas and necessary repeated port names. Production headings, page references, status, provenance, instructions and caption paragraphs stay outside the art. An optional tiny line-style key can say "Model relation", "Condition", and "Association". Use short local labels, not sentences on global arrows.

REFERENCE ADAPTATION AND FINAL SCIENTIFIC CHECK

Borrow only composition principles from the inspected "From Forest to Farm" overview: a dominant detailed physical scene, asymmetric supporting regions, a cutaway that exposes internal operations, and local objects large enough to read. Do not borrow its ecological organisms, soil layers, color-to-species mapping, arrow semantics, or food-web topology. The inspected source paper's page-4 overview contributes the recognition that performance, demand, finance, and constrained decisions belong to one transmission chain. Do not reproduce its equal method boxes, circular output cards, disconnected risk sidebar, or bottom dashboard strip. The arena and accounting geometry specified here determine this figure's identity. No other reference's scientific claims or experimental imagery belong here.

Inspect with headings hidden: seats still expose censoring; tail mass survives at the cap; tickets multiply quantity and price; the ledger has correct signs and subtotals; b and q post to both stocks; V remains separate from cash; actions alter specific operands; future observations cannot inform earlier choices.

Produce one complete conceptual draft. All unnumbered geometric marks are symbolic, not measured evidence. Add no empirical plots, numerical totals, optimized prices, calibrated capacities, confidence intervals, branding or validation claims. Use detail for the seat boundary, demand support, matched receipts, accounting operands and persistent states. The result is a scientific cutaway of a club's operations, with its arena connected to its books and decisions.

Edit the supplied white arena-and-accounting scientific illustration. Preserve the detailed arena, all main objects, title, capacity inset, two cash/debt equations and their signs, valuations, roster/time arrangement, and all correct formulas. Make only these precise scientific connector/operand corrections.

1. Inside the operating ledger, replace the sequence 'Debt D → Rate r → I_D' with two independent INPUTS. Put Debt D and Rate r side by side without any arrow between them. Each has its own short arrow into one multiplication sign, whose output is I_D = D × r. Connect I_D to the ledger's −I_D subtraction row, below EBI. Nothing implies debt determines the interest rate. In the top-right valuation leaves, remove the arrow from DCF down to r; r is an external condition and its dashed arrows must point FROM r TO discounting on the valuation leaves and TO the separate interest calculation. No arrow from r stops at the accounting title.

2. The ticket-receipt subtotal T_ticket = 10⁻⁶ Σ_home Â_t p̄_t must have one short solid arrow whose tip lands on the first '+ T_ticket' entry IN the ledger. Remove the old dashed connection that stops on the ledger's top border. Route around the title through the clear left margin. Ticket revenue must not directly enter EBI, profit or the cash row.

3. In the lower-left demand inset, remove the orange floating dot below/right of the capacity C_t. Keep the original latent-demand density and dashed censored tail unchanged. Add a short separate horizontal 'Attendance' support line immediately beneath the demand axis, sharing the EXACT horizontal C_t position with the original vertical cap. Place the orange probability-mass dot on this lower support line AT C_t, not to its right. A tiny local label says P(D_t ≥ C_t | x_t). Keep that probability label distinct from the expected-value operand C_t P(D_t ≥ C_t | x_t). Below the supports, retain the correct expectation decomposition E[D_t 1(D_t<C_t)|x_t] + C_t P(D_t≥C_t|x_t) → Â_t with its plus sign. Reflow this small inset locally as needed so the formula is clean and not overlapped by the new support line. No physical seats or forecast appear beyond C_t.

4. In the NO_MOVE action record explicitly show all three zero increments: ΔE=0, ΔP=0, ΔS=0. Keep SIGN/TRADE symbolic without made-up values. Remove the arena facade's 'INDIANA FEVER' text, leaving a plain architectural strip; no new branding or team logo.

Keep the pure white background and restrained linework. Do not add data, monetary amounts, new accounting items, or a new model.

Preserve the selected detailed arena, seat enlargement, lower demand distribution and tail atom, all formulas, cash/debt signs, valuations, pricing context and roster/time sequence. 1. Delete the incomplete blue connector below the home-ticket subtotal near the top-left edge of the ledger. It currently begins in empty space and runs into the header area.
